title: Bean initialization and shutdown
summary: Initialization order, Jakarta imports, startup hooks, and shutdown boundaries.

sources.title: Engineering Digest: Mastering @PostConstruct in Spring Boot: Complete Guide for Developers
Spring Framework: initialization and destruction callbacks
Spring Boot: application events and listeners
Official reference: Bean initialization and shutdown

richText: For a normal bean, Spring constructs the object, supplies its dependencies, then calls its initialization callbacks.
Constructor-injected dependencies are available in the constructor. Field-injected dependencies are supplied afterward.
@PostConstruct marks a method to call after dependency injection. Use jakarta.annotation.PostConstruct with Spring Boot 3.
Initialization runs when that bean instance is initialized. It does not run for every HTTP request.

example.title: Initialize a bean after dependency injection
description: This bean uses an injected Clock to record when initialization occurs.
explanation: Register the Clock bean shown in the beans lesson.
Spring supplies Clock before calling initialize().
The stored time belongs to this bean instance; getInitializedAt() does not refresh it.

richText: CommandLineRunner and ApplicationRunner run after the application context has been initialized. They receive application arguments in different forms.
ApplicationReadyEvent is published after the startup runners complete. It is a startup event, not a recurring timer.
@PostConstruct is not a transaction boundary. Transactional proxy behavior may not be available during initialization.
A remote operation during initialization delays startup. Give it a timeout if startup depends on it.
@PreDestroy marks a cleanup method called when Spring destroys a managed bean during normal context shutdown.
Abrupt termination can prevent cleanup callbacks from running or completing.
Spring does not automatically call destruction callbacks for prototype-scoped beans after handing them to the caller.
